questions.q: What do we learn by observing objects around us?
questions.a: Their materials, colours, shapes and uses - the first step of science.

questions.q: Name three objects and one property of each.
questions.a: Glass: transparent. Iron nail: hard, lustrous. Sponge: soft, squeezable.

questions.q: How do properties decide an object's use?
questions.a: We pick materials by property - glass for windows (transparent), metal for pans (conducts heat).

questions.q: On what basis can materials be grouped?
questions.a: Lustre, hardness, solubility in water, floating, and transparency.

questions.q: Group wood, glass and iron by any one property.
questions.a: Transparency: glass is transparent; wood and iron are opaque.
Similar materials can be studied together and the right one chosen for each job.

questions.q: Why is a tumbler not made of cloth?
questions.a: A tumbler must hold water - cloth soaks and leaks; glass or steel suits.

questions.q: Name the properties that make steel good for utensils.
questions.a: It conducts heat, is hard, shiny and does not break easily.

questions.q: Give one material that is transparent and used at home.
questions.a: Glass (windows, tumblers) - it lets us see through.
Anything that has mass and takes up space - all materials around us are matter.

questions.q: Name the three states of matter with examples.
Is air matter even though we cannot see it?
questions.a: Yes - it has mass and fills space (a balloon blown up weighs more).
